text:
devon: heads up — nsys trace from the evening run shows a repeated HBM bandwidth spike tied to kv_read kernels when seq_len > 6k. suspecting a prefetch window interaction with our batching heuristics. attaching quick snippets below.

lei: ugh, saw higher p99 on canary too. did this start after the kernel-selection tweak last week?

samir: yep, the dispatch path was changed to prefer the coalesced-read kernel for long sequences (PR #4123). i thought that reduced kernel latency, but maybe it increases HBM pressure when many microbatches align.

maria: can you paste the nsys summary? short snippets are fine.

devon: pasted short excerpt from nsys (trimmed):
```
GPU activities:  89.4%  kv_read (coalesced)
Memory copy:    7.1%  cudaMemcpyAsync
Other kernels:  3.5%
HBM BW: peaks at 780 GB/s during kv_read windows
Kernel timeline: repeated bursts every ~12ms correlated with batch boundary
```

perf-bot: note: recent regression alert for model serving p99 increased by ~18% on weekdays. Link: https://perf.redwood/alerts/2026-02-kv-hbm-spike

lei: that timeline is interesting — bursts every 12ms sounds like synchronized microbatch flush. are we flushing caches on batch boundary?

samir: our batching heuristic groups requests into groups of N up to 64 or until T ms, whichever first. when traffic is steady we hit N concurrently often. if sequence lengths are large, each microbatch causes large kv walking that saturates HBM.

aj: quick experiment idea: randomize the prefetch window start by jitter in [0..microbatch_window) to de-synchronize read waves. also try smaller max-batch for sequences > threshold.

maria: can we reproduce locally with perfetto so we can get a flamechart? i can run a 4-A100 perfetto capture if someone provides a reproducible driver.

devon: ran 3 quick experiments this morning:
- baseline (coalesced kernel, batch=64): p50 18ms, p95 92ms, p99 210ms
- jittered-prefetch (random offset 0..12ms): p50 19ms, p95 78ms, p99 130ms
- smaller-batch for longseq (max-batch=24 if seq>4k): p50 20ms, p95 75ms, p99 125ms
Observations: jitter reduced p99 a lot, lowers HBM peak by ~25% (from nsys snapshots).

lei: nice. does jitter hurt throughput overall?

samir: small drop in aggregated throughput (~3%) but p99 improvement looks good for SLOs. tradeoff seems favorable.

maria: i'll schedule perfetto on the nightly dedicated cluster and capture a 60s window with and without jitter. can we get a trace id to compare?

ops-bot: started perfetto job on cluster-dedicated-03, trace id: trace-2026-02-08-8487. ETA 45m.

devon: next steps: (1) add opt-in randomized prefetch jitter to runtime (config flag), (2) add heuristic to reduce max-batch for seq_len > 4096, (3) run full perfetto + nsys comparison and produce small commit with metrics.

aj: +1. can we also add a short A/B in Canary for 24h to confirm real traffic? if perf looks stable we can promote.

maria: i'll handle the perfetto captures and generate perfheat + flamecharts. will post links here when done.

lei: i'll add a small test to the microbenchmark harness: run 1000 requests with randomized jitter enabled and measure HBM BW via nsys sampling.

samir: i'll draft the config flag PR and the batch-size heuristic. leaving it unforced; we'll enable in canary only.

devon: thanks — keeping this thread for the artifacts. please ping if anyone hits regressions while canary is running. :thumbsup:
